method: Retained unchanged source labels for surviving claims; independently inspected every newly sampled source and enclosing control flow against the published criteria. Historical before labels and report are retained beside this artifact.

criteria.D001: A nontrivial normalized function body is duplicated within the reported class/module grouping. Published pass/empty-return hook exclusions apply. Distinct defaults, intentional abstract hooks and repeated test fixtures are classified explicitly; semantic equivalence and refactor usefulness are not claimed.
criteria.B006: The broad caught failure has no normally visible reporting, forwarding or subsequently checked error channel. Expected-exception assertions and checked thread/callback state are visible consumers. Debug-only logs and unasserted counters do not count.
criteria.I001: An imported binding has no code, annotation or explicit export use. Quoted annotations count. Side-effect/removal safety is a separate question.

labels.reason: Both bodies return convert(key, key). The distinct default conversion maps are deliberate contextual differences; this verifies body duplication only, not semantic interchangeability.
Both decorated tasks raise the same Exception body. Decorator retry settings differ, but the rule claims body duplication only.
The two local add tasks return x + y; distinct surrounding tests do not change their body text.
Both methods delegate to _stop_nodes with the same named arguments. Different retry defaults are deliberate over-inclusion, not a claim that the methods are interchangeable.
The two errback hooks contain the same nonempty dictionary return. Shared body text is real; keeping separate test fixtures can be intentional.
Both handlers call self._log_error with task, req and a new ExceptionInfo. The duplicated body is present in source.
Both autoretry task bodies increment iterations and divide a by b; decorator policy differs outside the body.

Both base-backend hooks return the result parameter. The documented trivial-literal/empty-return exemption does not include parameter passthrough; classify this as intentional structural over-inclusion.
Both task bodies return x / y. The different base-task decorators are outside the claimed body comparison.
Both abstract schedule hooks raise NotImplementedError(). This body is deliberately repeated for independent override points; the documented no-op exemption does not cover raises.
Both task fixtures return x * y. The body match is real; separate test fixtures do not establish refactoring value.
Both worker-component methods close w.hub. The two lifecycle names do not change the duplicated statement.
This local add task and the earlier add_with_before_start both return x + y; repeated fixtures are body duplicates.
Both result-consumer abstract methods raise NotImplementedError(). Deliberate override-point repetition is an over-inclusion mechanism, not a body-extraction error.
Both signature hooks assign self.msg_id to mtask_id and return it under the same dictionary key.
Both abstract result-consumer methods raise NotImplementedError(); different parameters are outside the normalized body claim.
Both hooks return the identical nonempty header dictionary. The source supports the normalized body claim.
Both abstract result-consumer methods raise NotImplementedError(). Preserve the deliberate-over-inclusion classification.
Both fake-hub helpers raise OSError. The statements are duplicated; intentional test failure fixtures are not automatically candidates for refactoring.
Both decorated retry tasks increment iterations and return a + b; body duplication is source-visible.
The reconnect handler only writes a debug-level log. Failure detail remains invisible at the normal logging level under the published rule policy.
The handler increments exception_count, but that count is only printed at debug level and is never asserted. The memory assertion does not check whether the expected exceptions were observed.
The broad handler consists solely of pass, with no forwarding, report, or checked failure state.

A subsequent assertion verifies that BRPOP was armed, but does not explicitly observe the caught exception. The source alone does not prove whether every tolerated connection error is checked or silently lost.
The handler substitutes stamps=None and provides no diagnostic or explicit failure-state assertion. Computed defaults do not disclose the caught failure.
The warm-up handler is pass-only. Its intentional tolerance is not a visible diagnostic under the stated B006 policy.
The handler replaces children with None without reporting the exception or marking an analysis failure.
The broad import fallback sets posix to None and provides no visible failure signal.
The reconnect close handler only uses logger.debug with exc_info. The default logging level does not expose this failure.
The broad thread.wait handler contains only pass; the caught failure is not asserted or reported in that handler.
The broad retry memory-loop handler contains pass and no visible failure signal.
The broad task-success memory-loop handler contains pass and no visible failure signal.
The broad nested-stack memory-loop handler contains pass and no visible failure signal.
AQLQueryError is imported and assigned in the dependency-fallback branch but never read or exported. The __all__ list exports only ArangoDbBackend.

The couchbase binding is never read. The same module independently calls pytest.importorskip("couchbase"), so this label verifies unused binding only and does not treat arbitrary side-effect imports as removable.
